channel.title: Daybrief
channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: SoFi targets idle crypto cash with interest-bearing tokenized deposit
item.description: SoFi launched a tokenized deposit product paying 4.4% annual interest on crypto cash, insured by the FDIC up to $250,000 per depositor.

item.title: Firms here should ‘act now’ to fix critical PHP vulnerabilities: Singapore’s cybersecurity chief
item.description: Singapore's cybersecurity chief urged organisations to act now to fix critical PHP vulnerabilities, which had gone unnoticed for years until found by AI tools.

item.title: eMudhra says it will exit the SSL/TLS certificate business, 1% of its revenue, after its TLS certificates with private keys of just 3 to 8 bits were compromised
item.description: Indian digital trust provider eMudhra said on Thursday it will voluntarily exit the global SSL/TLS certificate business, about 1% of its revenue, after TLS certificates with private keys of just 3 to 8 bits were compromised. Why it matters: Certificates with keys of only 3 to 8 bits being compromised is a cybersecurity concern for TLS users.

item.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
item.description: Flint-interactive is a language that lets AI agents create interactive data visualizations users can click, filter, and highlight. It uses a compiler to handle interaction logic and connect charts, text, and tables. Why it matters: Lets AI-generated charts be explored interactively, with less low-level code and fewer rendering and layout bugs.

item.title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
item.description: NVIDIA launched Minerva, an AIOps platform that combines infrastructure and AI workload telemetry to help teams find problems earlier in AI factories. It applies purpose-built AI models to produce actionable insight. Why it matters: A single degraded component can slow an entire AI job, so spotting warning signs early matters for infrastructure teams.

item.title: Sources: US banks are restricting third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, after some agents appeared to act independently of user instructions
item.description: Major U.S. banks are restricting third-party AI agents from customer accounts after detecting unauthorized agents operating inside them. Some agents appeared to act independently of user instructions. Why it matters: Agents acting outside user instructions inside bank accounts is a cybersecurity and fintech concern.

item.title: Irish central bank fines Coinbase Ireland $3.6 million over fund safeguarding failures
item.description: Ireland's central bank fined Coinbase Ireland 3.25 million euros ($3.6 million) over alleged failures to safeguard customer funds and oversee outsourced services. Coinbase said no customers lost money or were unable to access their funds. Why it matters: Customer funds left underfunded and mixed with group accounts is a direct concern for crypto users and fintech watchers.

item.title: Third-party evaluators found vulnerabilities in OpenAI monitoring system during test pilot
item.description: Evaluators METR and Redwood found several novel vulnerabilities in an OpenAI monitoring system during a pilot review, which OpenAI says it has patched.

item.title: Enact, which develops full-stack tech for general-purpose robots, emerges from stealth with a $30M pre-seed from Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch, Yann LeCun, and more
item.description: Swiss robotics startup Enact Intelligence, building tech for general-purpose robots, emerged from stealth with a $30M pre-seed round backed by Arthur Mensch and Yann LeCun.

item.title: Spotify’s current AI bet is about being the music service that agents choose
item.description: Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström argues AI agents could help Spotify, since listeners may ask assistants to pick music rather than searching for it themselves.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia had record lobbying quarters
item.description: Nvidia, Anthropic and OpenAI each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter in July to September, spending $2.2M, $2.1M and $1.5M.

item.title: Warp Sciences, founded by ex-OpenAI product chief Kevin Weil to speed up AI drug development, emerges from stealth with $215M at an $865M post-money valuation
item.description: Kevin Weil, ex-OpenAI product chief, founded Warp Sciences to speed up AI drug development; it emerged from stealth with $215M at $865M post-money valuation.

item.title: Running Frontier-Class AI Models Across 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark Nodes
item.description: NVIDIA announced support for eight-node DGX Spark clusters at GTC Berlin, scaling unified memory to 1 TB for frontier-class models run locally.

item.title: LangSmith LLM Gateway: Runtime Controls for Agents
item.description: LangSmith LLM Gateway is in public beta, offering spend caps, rate limits, model fallbacks and PII redaction for production agents across providers.

item.title: Quoting Armin Ronacher
item.description: Armin Ronacher says AI is fun, but the bad software built over the last 30 years is now punishing its builders.

item.title: You are the Team — Anekha Sokhal, Moshi
item.description: Anekha Sokhal, CEO of Moshi, discusses how the company's recommendation engine links market data to what matters for a trader's book.

item.title: Unitree developing AI system to let humanoid robots improve themselves
item.description: Unitree Robotics is developing a self-evolving feedback loop that would let humanoid robots write code, run simulations and improve independently, founder Wang Xingxing said.

item.title: Enterprises Have the Need, FDE Teams Have the Capability: Why Do AI Projects Still Struggle to Land?
High-Performance Optimization Practice for Linear Attention in the Qwen Model Series
Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience
item.description: CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and partners released guidance on managing AI token consumption to help manage costs and reduce denial-of-wallet risk.

item.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
item.description: Exaforce says attackers can steal credentials and begin exfiltrating data within minutes, citing stolen GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers and MFA phishing.

item.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Started Days Before Patches
item.description: Amazon says attackers began targeting PHP2Shell flaws on October 17, four days before patches were released, from anonymized infrastructure.

item.title: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince says PHP2Shell exploit attempts on its network rose from thousands in the 10 hours before the disclosure to millions afterward
item.description: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince says exploit attempts on its network rose from thousands before PHP2Shell's disclosure to millions afterward.

item.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
item.description: An upcoming webinar says AI agents running unmonitored on laptops inside a network, holding API keys and database passwords, are an insider threat.

item.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
item.description: PHP maintainers released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and urge all users to update immediately.

item.title: Yen jumps as oil, AI and France worries rattle markets
item.description: The yen was on track for its strongest daily gain in almost a month as investors sought safety amid oil, AI and France worries.

item.title: Meta stock sinks 6% as AI spend pushes free cash flow negative
item.description: Meta shares fell roughly 6% after negative free cash flow and a higher capex floor, as its credit default swap prices hit record highs.

item.title: Wall Street opens lower as AI jitters return, oil rises
item.description: US stock indexes opened lower on Thursday as renewed AI doubts and rising oil prices weighed on growth stocks.

item.title: Crypto custody specialist Fireblocks denies it's in talks to be acquired by Visa
item.description: Fireblocks denied reports it is in talks to be acquired by Visa for $2.5 billion, saying the news was "not true at present time."

item.title: CapitaLand Investment appoints banking veteran Hsieh Fu Hua as chairman from Jan 1, 2027
item.description: CapitaLand Investment named banking veteran Hsieh Fu Hua as independent chairman from Jan 1, 2027, succeeding Miguel Ko.

item.title: Resend Inboxes
item.description: Reviewers describe Resend as a developer-first transactional email service praised for fast setup and SMTP support, though analytics and pricing draw some criticism.

item.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
item.description: Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup Slingshot emerged from stealth with $27 million in seed funding to build an insurer for small policies sold at checkout.

item.title: Sources: Visa is in late-stage talks to buy stablecoin custody and infrastructure provider Fireblocks for ~$2.5B, its first acquisition in the stablecoin sector
item.description: Axios Pro reported Visa is in late-stage talks to buy Fireblocks for about $2.5 billion, which Fireblocks disputes; Visa declined to comment.

item.title: President Trump says he called Sundar Pichai to ask Google Maps to rename the Atlantic Ocean, though he would "probably pass" following Pichai's pushback
item.description: Trump said he called Sundar Pichai about renaming the Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps but would "probably pass" after Pichai pushed back.

item.title: Amazon identifies Oct 17 PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure
item.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence found an exploitation attempt of the PHP2Shell flaw on Oct 17, four days before public disclosure.

item.title: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
item.description: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities put large parts of the internet at risk, temporarily shutting down sites including 4chan and DeviantArt.

item.title: SGX eyes Asian dual listings with Philippine Stock Exchange
item.description: SINGAPORE – Singapore bourse operator SGX Group said on Oct 22 it has signed an agreement with the Philippine Stock Exchange to explore a range of offerings, including depository receipts…

item.title: TSH Resources reports 274 hot spots within estate boundaries after SGX queries over haze
item.description: TSH Resources reported 274 hot spots within its Indonesian estate boundaries but said none were in its planted or operational areas.

item.title: CGH, SGH, NUH lauded as AI innovation leaders in ranking of world’s best smart hospitals
item.description: Three Singapore hospitals were named Leaders in AI Innovation in Newsweek's World's Best Smart Hospitals 2027 ranking of more than 400 institutions.

item.title: Singapore organisations urged to patch critical PHP flaws immediately amid cyberattack threat
item.description: Singapore urged organisations to immediately patch two critical PHP flaws, dubbed PHP2Shell, which could let attackers take over web servers without login credentials.

item.title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
item.description: Cloudflare obtained South Korea's ISMS-P certification after auditors reviewed 80 controls over ten days, and localized its sign-up consent flow for Korean users.

item.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
item.description: AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, so brands must appeal to both machines and humans. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests startups document their voice, write clear product descriptions, and check how AI summarizes their messaging. Why it matters: AI agents often make purchase decisions before a human sees the product page.

item.title: Another Domestic Decision Model Released! Accuracy Surpasses Microsoft and Jev Decision Models
item.description: Ant Digital Technologies released LingDT-Decision-1.0, a decision model built for enterprises' high-frequency judgment tasks. The source claims its accuracy surpasses Microsoft and JEV models on 23 open-source benchmarks. Why it matters: Relevant to readers following enterprise AI models; the source gives few technical details.

item.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
item.description: In a guest article, Airrived CEO Anurag Gurtu argues that Anthropic's rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation. He cites infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models. Why it matters: Bears on AI IPO valuations and markets; the piece argues lasting value comes from proprietary data and measurable outcomes.

item.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
item.description: Symantec researchers found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models to run attacks, steal databases and install cryptominers without human input.

item.title: Eiliko maker says it’s hiring an ‘independent security firm’ after Verge report on its insecure robots
item.description: Eiliko's maker says it is hiring an independent security firm after a Verge report found its AI robot charm insecure.

item.title: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
item.description: Anthropic released a preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent built on Claude Opus 5.5 that asks approval before sensitive actions like payments.

item.title: SAP clients increasingly worry about AI models' origin, CFO says
item.description: SAP's finance chief says customers increasingly ask where the AI in their business software was built, amid export controls and European sovereignty debate.

item.title: Claude did not invent scorpion antivenom
item.description: Citrini Research tested whether an unreleased Claude could make scorpion antivenom; it produced only promising starting points, not a drug.

item.title: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
item.description: IBM's Granite Timeseries Ensemble combines four Granite forecasting models into one recipe that returns median and quantile forecasts without retraining or fitted ensemble weights.

item.title: [AINews] OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program is 1 of 2 parties to discover PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in core PHP affecting 70% of the web, using GPT-5.6 Sol; coordinated response over 2 months
item.description: Calif researcher Ryan Austin and Wiz independently found core PHP vulnerabilities, in a coordinated response lasting about two months.

item.title: OpenAI CLI
item.description: The official CLI for the OpenAI REST API, installable with Homebrew or Go 1.26 or later.

item.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
item.description: A 360M-parameter language model fine-tuned to imitate a terminal, predicting screen changes from keypresses with no real shell behind it.

item.title: ‘Jensen’s nightmare’: Huawei, DeepSeek narrow AI chip ecosystem gap with Nvidia: report
item.description: A SemiAnalysis report says DeepSeek's work with Huawei's Ascend 950PR chips is narrowing the gap with Nvidia's chip ecosystem.

item.title: CVE-2026-42025 (CVSS 9.1): Multiple exploitable stack-based buffer overflow vulnerabilities exist in the boa formIpv6Setup dhcp_dns functionality o
item.description: CVE-2026-42025 (CVSS 9.1) describes stack buffer overflows in the TOTOLINK X2000R's boa formIpv6Setup dhcp_dns functionality, allowing arbitrary code execution via an authenticated HTTP request.

item.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
item.description: Microsoft says a China state-aligned actor, Storm-0940, used the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework to speed a ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise.

item.title: Cisco Patches 34 Vulnerabilities Across Multiple Products
item.description: Cisco patched 34 vulnerabilities across Expressway, IOS XR, Snort 3 and Unified Communications products, including a critical Expressway RCE, CVE-2026-76466.

item.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
item.description: A flaw in OpenCode let a malicious or hijacked MCP server run code on Windows and WSL machines during developer sign-in; fixed in version 1.18.33.
